messages:
IncidentBot: Pager alert: spike in 5xxs for /v1/prompt-route (new-endpoint) — error-rate 18% over 2m, latency p95 -> 1.4s. alert_id=INC-2184521 :rotating_light:
Maya Chen: seeing it on the dashboard too. Canary cluster version=prompt-new-route-v2. Canary traffic target was 5% but traffic jumped to ~20% in last 4m.
Raj Patel: noted. I'm pulling logs now. Any customer reports?
Eli Gordon: ops-external reported increased error traces from two sandbox customers. No enterprise P1s yet.
Tamara Vega: I can flip the FF if needed. Which flag controls routing to v2?
Maya Chen: flag is prompt_new_route_v2 (prod scope). Toggle path: /flags/prompt_new_route_v2 -> set false.
Raj Patel: pulling recent deploy history: canary roll started at 2184520540, autoscaler increased canary percentage due to health-check mis-tagging.
Oncall Pager: paging oncall_empirical (primary oncall) — page sent.
Maya Chen: log snippet from canary instances: ```
[ERR] kv_cache_miss: downstream timeout (deadline exceeded) id=7f3a
[ERR] serve_loop: unexpected EOF from model backend
```
Raj Patel: looks like backend pool (model-backend-nvidia-6) had a transient kernel OOM and restarted; health-checks flapped and auto-scaler moved more traffic to canary nodes.
Eli Gordon: customer impact: ~3% of total production requests saw 500s, concentrated on short-sequence chat endpoints. Approx ~1500 requests/min at peak.
Maya Chen: recommendation: engage kill-switch on flag to route all traffic back to stable endpoint, hold canary at 0% and drain v2. That should stop errors.
Tamara Vega: agree. I'm ready to flip. Confirming with SRE before touching prod.
Raj Patel: confirm. Also add circuit-breaker to drop new long-running requests while we revert. Command for FF service: ```
curl -X POST "https://console.redwood.internal/flags/toggle" -d '{"flag":"prompt_new_route_v2","value":false,"actor":"TamaraV"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
```
Tamara Vega: executing now.
Tamara Vega: done — flag prompt_new_route_v2 set to false. API returned 200. rollout_id=r-2184521
Maya Chen: seeing immediate drop in traffic to v2 clusters. Error rate falling. p95 latency trending down.
IncidentBot: Auto-check: flag change detected by rollout-watcher. Re-evaluating traffic split: stable=100%, canary=0% (propagated in ~12s).
Eli Gordon: starting manual drain of canary: `/bin/drain-canary --cluster prompt-new-route-v2 --grace 30s`
Raj Patel: collecting for postmortem: why autoscaler increased canary beyond intended 5% — suspect health-check label mismatch on new instances. Also add question of kernel OOMs on model-backend-nvidia-6.
Maya Chen: customer comms: two sandbox customers reported timeouts, no enterprise P1s. We'll prepare a short note: "We've rolled back canary routing due to increased errors; stable routing restored; investigating root cause; will follow up."
Oncall Pager: primary oncall accepted handoff. paging note added to incident.
Tamara Vega: canary is drained. cluster instances marked for debug and removed from LB.
IncidentBot: Metrics check in 60s scheduled.
Raj Patel: preliminary impact estimate: incident duration ~6m from first spike to kill-switch, approx 0.8% error-rate delta on 5m window for overall traffic, localized to prompt-route path: up to 18% 5xx in the canary subset.
Eli Gordon: I ran quick `kubectl logs` and captured OOM trace; uploading to artifact store: https://artifacts.internal/2184521/oom-traces.log
Maya Chen: next actions: 1) SRE to investigate autoscaler policy + health-check tags; 2) Runtime team to inspect kernel OOMs on model-backend pool; 3) Product to validate routing tests for canary gating; 4) Draft customer follow-up. Assigning owners in thread.
Raj Patel: I'll lead autoscaler/health-check postmortem.
Eli Gordon: I'll own runtime OOM triage.
Tamara Vega: I'll prepare the customer note and keep comms open.
Maya Chen: handoff: I'm off to run the follow-up meeting in 15m. Oncall will continue monitoring. If errors recur, re-open and we can re-engage flag.
Oncall Pager: monitoring active. No new errors in last 90s, overall system stabilizing.
Maya Chen: thanks all. short incident report to follow in incidents channel. :white_check_mark:
